text:
The talk around Sidney Crosby this week is about his future more than his game. NHL.com ran "Crosby knows Penguins need turnaround to keep veteran core intact," Daily Faceoff asked "Will Sidney Crosby ever move on from the Penguins?", and it also passed along Drake Batherson saying Crosby "can have my house" if he comes to the Senators. That is the backdrop for a 39-year-old captain on a team that needs to start winning.

On the ice, 14 points (6 goals) in 21 games at 19.6 minutes a night is a quieter start than last season's 74 points. His scoring rate, 2.04 points per 60, sits below our talent range for him (2.45 to 3.28), and Pittsburgh has scored 3.8 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him out there. That reads more like bounces than decline: the Penguins still take 53% of the 5v5 shot attempts with him on.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season. The setup work is what we'd watch. Our range for his season: 61 to 87 points.
